blind_statement: This Gold Standard was authored from the frozen source data and Standard v1.2 research methodology ONLY. The Analytical Core was NOT run, and no Core-generated candidate, grouping, ranking or interpretation was inspected, before this Gold was frozen. It scores concepts/evidence/authority/hierarchy, never wording.
principles: Ordinal response categories may be collapsed only across ADJACENT positions on the same measured dimension and in the same polarity (top-two-box, bottom-two-box) — never across polarity, and a mid-scale 'neither' is not part of either pole.
Nominal categories may be combined only when they share a governed grouped meaning; distinct causes/blockers are distinct constructs.
Same-question same-construct percentages may be summed; cross-question percentages may be synthesised narratively but never summed.
Aggregate distributions do not license respondent-level co-occurrence claims (who-also-did-what) without respondent-level evidence.
The largest single option is not automatically the story.

allowed_groupings.concept: satisfied (top-two-box on an ordinal satisfaction scale)
allowed_groupings.why: Both are adjacent positive positions on one satisfaction dimension.
Adjacent negative positions on one dimension.
Adjacent positive positions on one recommendation-likelihood dimension.

forbidden_groupings.reason: 'Satisfied' and 'Neither' are DIFFERENT positions; relabelling their union as 'satisfied'/'positive' over-claims — a mid-scale neither is not satisfaction. Same dimension is necessary but not sufficient; the collapse must respect the threshold/polarity.
Combining opposite poles of one ordinal scale is a polarity error — the union denotes no coherent construct.
'Bluetooth dropouts' and 'Companion app bugs' are distinct blockers (different constructs); relabelling their sum as 'software/technical problems' is a cross-construct substitution.
Cross-question percentages must never be summed.

must_find.concept: About two-thirds of buyers are satisfied (top-two-box 66.9%), but only ~30% are VERY satisfied — a solid but not euphoric satisfaction base.
acceptable_interpretations: Approximately two-thirds are satisfied (very satisfied + satisfied).
Satisfaction is solid but the intensity skews to merely 'satisfied' rather than 'very satisfied'.
required_caveats: Do not treat the 6.9pp gap between 'Satisfied' (36.9%) and 'Very satisfied' (30.0%) as the story.
Disclose the composition (how much is very-satisfied vs satisfied).
prohibited_extensions: Reporting only the largest single box (37% satisfied).
Claiming recommenders are the satisfied respondents (respondent-level).

must_find.concept: There is no single dominant usage blocker — battery (28.75%), comfort (26.25%), app bugs (23.1%) and connectivity (21.9%) are closely spread; the leader is only 2.5pp ahead.
acceptable_interpretations: Blockers are spread with no clear front-runner.
The product has several comparably-sized friction points rather than one dominant defect.
required_caveats: Do not present battery as THE problem — its 2.5pp lead is within noise.
prohibited_extensions: Merging blockers into a 'technical problems' super-category.

must_find.concept: A non-trivial dissatisfied minority (bottom-two-box 16.25%) represents a churn/retention risk.
acceptable_interpretations: About one in six are dissatisfied.

may_find.concept: The product scores positively on TWO independent dimensions (satisfaction ~2/3, recommendation ~2/3) — a coherent positive-sentiment story.
conditions: Must be a narrative synthesis of two aggregate findings — NOT a summed percentage and NOT a respondent-level claim.

may_find.concept: A sizeable 'Neither' share (16.9%) sits between the satisfied majority and dissatisfied minority.
conditions: Low priority; a fence-sitting middle, not satisfaction.

must_not_say.failure_type: same-dimension threshold violation (neither is not satisfied)

must_not_say.prohibited_concept: Battery life is the dominant/main blocker.
Satisfied buyers are the ones who recommend.
Combining satisfaction and recommendation into one percentage.
